humanities_elective.rule: Complete two courses from different clusters; PHI 220 is preferred but not required.

computer_science_engineering_elective.rule: Choose EGR 121, EGR 122, CSC 215, or another advisor-approved course for transfer purposes.
computer_science_engineering_elective.open_option: other course approved by the advisor for transfer purposes

unit_audit.computer_competency_rule: Graduates of programs containing 45 or more credits must meet the college computer competency requirement. ITE 115 plus an eligible SDV course is one automatic route; approved program activities or the competency test are alternate routes, so ITE 115 is not added to this curriculum.

residency.rule: At least 25 percent of the credits must be acquired at Wytheville Community College.

other_graduation_requirements: Fulfill every curriculum course and credit-hour requirement.
Earn at least a 2.0 GPA in applicable studies.
Apply for graduation by the published deadline.
Resolve college obligations and return college materials.
Receive certification by an appropriate college official.

analysis_constraints.description: The program directs students to complete community-college courses with a grade of C; the current evaluator does not enforce per-course grades.
Computer competency can be met through course, program-activity, or testing routes and must not be flattened into an extra ITE 115 course requirement.

modeling_notes: The current catalog labels the four term blocks a suggested sequence. This composition preserves every categorical course row and footnote option but intentionally excludes the prospective schedule labels.

History and Humanities rows carry misaligned printed footnote superscripts. Their unique category labels and the separately numbered definitions resolve them to the history and humanities menus without inventing an option.

The two humanities slots are separate and must come from different clusters. The current program page supplies the seven-course union but does not publish a course-to-cluster dictionary, so that cross-choice rule remains explicit for human review.
The two physics slots use different closed menus: PHY 201 or PHY 241 first, followed by PHY 202 or PHY 242.

The advisor-approved transfer-course branch of the Computer Science/Engineering elective is retained as an open source constraint; the three named options remain directly accessible by deterministic course identity.

data_quality_flags.message: The first History and Humanities rows display superscripts 2 and 5 although the uniquely matching definitions are numbered 1 and 2.
The program requires different humanities clusters but does not map its seven eligible courses to cluster identities.
The Computer Science/Engineering elective includes a source-authorized advisor-approved transfer course outside the three named options.

The current VCCS master page shows CSC 221 as four credits effective 2026-08-01, while this current local degree page explicitly prints CSC 221 as three and closes the award at 62. The local degree requirement and published total are retained pending catalog correction.
